name: Cheesy French Onion Skillet White Beans

ingredients.name: yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced
kosher salt, plus more to taste
freshly ground black pepper, plus more for garnish
chopped fresh thyme leaves, plus more for garnish

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 205°C (400°F). In a large skillet, melt butter over medium-high heat until foaming. Add onions, salt, and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, 6 to 8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook, stirring frequently and scraping bottom of skillet with wooden spoon as needed to avoid scorching, until onions are sweet and deeply caramelized, about 45 minutes. If browned onion juices on bottom of skillet threaten to burn, add 1 tablespoon water, scrape up browned bits, and continue cooking.

While onions caramelize, arrange bread cubes in an even layer on a rimmed baking sheet and bake, stirring halfway through, until lightly toasted, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside. Set broiler to high.

Once onions are caramelized, add garlic and thyme to the onions and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add sherry, scraping up any browned bits with a wooden spoon, and cook over medium heat until alcohol is mostly evaporated, 1 to 2 minutes.

Add beans and broth and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Cook, stirring often, until beans are tender and broth is slightly thickened, about 7 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.
Top bean mixture evenly with toasted bread cubes, then sprinkle Gruyère and Parmigiano-Reggiano evenly over top. Broil until cheese is melted and browned in spots, about 2 minutes.
Garnish with thyme and black pepper. Serve immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: white bean dinner recipe, french onion soup recipe, French Onion Skillet White Beans

description: These French onion skillet beans combine creamy butter beans with deeply caramelized onions, savory broth, crisp baguette, and bubbling Gruyère for a cozy one-skillet dinner.
notes:
Optional substitutions: yellow onions → a mixture; homemade beef stock → chicken stock or vegetable stock

Notes: Yellow onions are the best all-purpose bet for this soup, but a mix of yellow, sweet (e.g., Vidalia), and red onions, plus shallots, creates an even more complex flavor.

Make-ahead and storage: The bean and onion base can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days before assembling and broiling to serve.
Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days, though the bread cubes will lose their crispness. Reheat in a 205°C (400°F) oven until warmed through.
author: Leah Colins
